(a) In General.—In the case of taxable years of a natural person beginning in 2005 or 2006, for purposes of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, taxable income shall be reduced by $500 for each Hurricane Katrina displaced individual of the taxpayer for the taxable year. 
    (b) Limitations.—
        (1) Dollar limitation.—The reduction under subsection (a) shall not exceed $2,000, reduced by the amount of the reduction under this section for all prior taxable years. 
        (2) Individuals taken into account only once.—An individual shall not be taken into account under subsection (a) if such individual was taken into account under such subsection by the taxpayer for any prior taxable year. 
        (3) Identifying information required.—An individual shall not be taken into account under subsection (a) for a taxable year unless the taxpayer identification number of such 
individual is included on the return of the taxpayer for such taxable year.   
    (c) Hurricane Katrina Displaced Individual.—For purposes of this section, the term “Hurricane Katrina displaced individual” means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, any natural person if—
        (1) such person’s principal place of abode on August 28, 2005, was in the Hurricane Katrina disaster area, 
        (2)
            (A) in the case of such an abode located in the core disaster area, such person is displaced from such abode, or 
            (B) in the case of such an abode located outside of the core disaster area, such person is displaced from such abode, and
                (i) such abode was damaged by Hurricane Katrina, or  
                (ii) such person was evacuated from such abode by reason of Hurricane Katrina, and   
        (3) such person is provided housing free of charge by the taxpayer in the principal residence of the taxpayer for a period of 60 consecutive days which ends in such taxable year.   Such term shall not include the spouse or any dependent of the taxpayer.
    (d) Compensation for Housing.—No deduction shall be allowed under this section if the taxpayer receives any rent or other amount (from any source) in connection with the providing of such housing.

fable.w: This section creates a tax deduction for taxpayers who housed people displaced by Hurricane Katrina and sets its limits and definitions. The tempting reading is that taxpayers interact with the government by putting identifying information on a return, but claiming a tax benefit is not consultation on a federal decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: taxable income shall be reduced by $500 for each Hurricane Katrina displaced individual of the taxpayer for the taxable year

opus.w: This section creates a tax reduction for taxpayers who house people displaced by Hurricane Katrina, and it defines who qualifies. Putting identifying information on a tax return is part of claiming a benefit, which the definition excludes. It is not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. No hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s:
An individual shall not be taken into account under subsection (a) for a taxable year unless the taxpayer identification number of such 
individual is included on the return of the taxpayer for such taxable year.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the taxpayer takes part in a federal process by filing a return with the displaced person's taxpayer identification number. That fails because filing a return to claim a tax reduction is like applying for a benefit, and the definition excludes that. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or new right to sue. It only sets the rules for who qualifies for the reduction and how much it is.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines eligibility criteria for a tax deduction related to Hurricane Katrina. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The interactions described are between taxpayers and displaced individuals, or between taxpayers and the IRS via tax returns, which are not forms of participation in federal decision-making as defined.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "Hurricane Katrina displaced individual" involves coordination with the displaced person (e.g., providing housing), but this is a condition for a tax benefit, not a participatory process in a federal decision. The statute defines eligibility criteria for a tax deduction. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with the public, states, or other outside entities before making a decision. The interaction is between the taxpayer and the displaced individual, and the taxpayer and the IRS (via filing a return). This falls under the exclusion for "applications for benefits" or simply statutory definitions of eligibility, not participation in decision-making.
